name: Question 9
problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=-2 \\ y+2z=-1 \\ z=11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=11$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+2(11)=-1\,⟹\,y=-23.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-23$ and $z=11$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(-23)+3(11)=-2\,⟹\,x=-58.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-58$, $y=-23$, and $z=11.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨-58,-23,11⟩.$

Question 9
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[−22−645−5161012−1].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨2,1,−1⟩
b
⟨52,21,−11⟩
c
⟨−2,−3,1⟩
d
⟨−58,−23,11⟩
e
⟨−3,−1,0⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[−22−645−5161012−1]R1:=−12R1∼[1−13−25−5161012−1]R2:=R2+(−5)R1∼[1−13−200111012−1].

Note that we get a22=0. Therefore, we swap the 2nd and 3rd rows:

M∼[1−13−200111012−1]R2↔R3∼[1−13−2012−100111]

So, the system is now

{x−y+3z=−2y+2z=−1z=11,

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation z=11 tells us the value of z. Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

y+2(11)=−1⟹y=−23.

Now, substituting y=−23 and z=11 into the first equation, we get

x−(−23)+3(11)=−2⟹x=−58.

Thus, the solution is x=−58, y=−23, and z=11. Or, in vector form, ⟨−58,−23,11⟩.
